The expression in the parenthesis is a perfect square, $(1+e^{i\theta})^2$.

We know that $|i|=1$ and $|e^{i\theta}| = |\cos\theta + i\sin\theta| = \sqrt{\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta} = 1$.
Also, for any complex number $w$, $|w^2| = |w|^2$. So, $|(1+e^{i\theta})^2| = |1+e^{i\theta}|^2$.
